question.prompt: Lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at point \(O\), and \(\angle AOC+\angle BOD=100^\circ\). What is the measure of \(\angle AOD\) in degrees?

solutions.explanation:
The answer depends on the directions of the named rays, which the statement does not specify. Each pair \(OA,OB\) and \(OC,OD\) can consist of the same ray or opposite rays.

If both pairs are opposite rays, \(\angle AOC\) and \(\angle BOD\) are vertical angles. Then \(\angle AOC=\angle BOD\), so \(\angle AOC=50^\circ\) and \(\angle AOD=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ\).

If both pairs are the same ray, the three named angles coincide. Place distinct \(A,B\) on one ray from \(O\), and distinct \(C,D\) on another ray making \(50^\circ\) with it. Then
\[
\angle AOC+\angle BOD=50^\circ+50^\circ=100^\circ,
\]
but \(\angle AOD=50^\circ\).

If exactly one pair is opposite, \(\angle AOC\) and \(\angle BOD\) sum to \(180^\circ\), so that case cannot satisfy the given sum. Thus the possible answers are \(50^\circ\) and \(130^\circ\). The key \(130^\circ\) requires the intended opposite-ray arrangement.
solutions.title: Check the possible point orders
